{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment is negative (sentiment < 0) or shows recent decline, as market cooling often leads to price correction.",
    "Reduce forecast magnitude after a sharp spike (e.g., >10% above recent mean) to avoid overreaction and prevent overshoot.",
    "Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is consistently above true outcome over 5+ days, reduce future forecasts by 5-10% to align with historical mean.",
    "Increase downward bias when true outcome is persistently below forecast, especially if sentiment is neutral or negative, to reflect market underperformance.",
    "For horizon > 10 days, reduce forecast volatility by smoothing out extreme outliers, as long-term trends often exhibit mean-reverting behavior.",
    "If sentiment is positive (sentiment > 0) and forecast is below true outcome, slightly increase forecast to capture sentiment-driven momentum.",
    "When true outcome is significantly below historical low (e.g., < 60% of 30-day average), apply a downward correction to avoid overestimating rebound potential."
  ]
}
